correctness.rationale: Strict convexity and coordinatewise KKT yield a unique threshold soft-shrinkage minimizer with residual tau independent of p for all real 1<p<infinity, r>0; inside the l1-ball it is identity. On each exterior sign/active-set cell, differentiation gives a sign-conjugate of C_k=I-11^T/k. Continuity and finite polyhedral cell decomposition bound the global Lipschitz quotient by max(1,||C_k||_p), while open full-dimensional cells realize every active k and any maximizing direction. C2 is contractive in every p, Ck orthogonal when p=2. The zero-mean vector (1,1,-2) and perturbation by constants gives strict amplification when p!=2 and n>=3. In k=3,p=4 the zero-sum quartic identity reduces maximizing ||C3 x||_4 to a quadratic constrained by sum x_i^4; Lagrange cubic gives only two-equal-coordinate extremizers above 1, then sharp weighted Hölder gives L^4=(1+2^(1/3))^3/9, numerically 1.0641658628581188. Duality covers p=4/3.
